route_status.proven_scope: The exact Godot 4.7.2-stable probe_opera_2d ran once with an isolated profile and returned OPERA2D|result: ALL OK. The source maps Magician TRACK to pearl_tide_pool and ROPE to teal_shell_stage; probe log checks the phase invitation art/glow/touch target for clipping and Roshan overlap, and checks that correct TRACK choices advance the target and start a fresh shuffle.
route_status.route_gaps: The assigned probe is a headless SceneTree test that directly sets world phase, task, surface and gesture state (scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:620-644); it does not walk a child through fresh-save Opera Hall entry, visible portal selection, rendered travel/opening, real finger contact, sound playback, full completion/exit/re-entry, or a child-paced session. The 112-pixel room invitation minimum and scripted state assertions do not establish Mobile composition, physical M11 touch tolerance, frame pacing, comprehension, fun, exact voice match/listening, or owner acceptance. Probe wall time is not gameplay duration. The approved run is for current source/runtime only; external and visual acceptance stays pending under MA-OPERA-004 and MA-OPERA-012. Lamba's semantic voice/visual mismatch remains blocked externally under MA-ACCESS-002.

code_constants.scope: Source timer, not an observed activity duration.

code_constants.scope: Progress units/configuration, not seconds. This review did not measure child completion time.

timing.assumptions: No child-paced activity duration was observed; receipt wall_elapsed_seconds measures the scripted probe process only.

tactile.target_size: OperaWorldHotspot2D enforces a minimum 112×112 canvas-pixel invitation hit target; probe checks Magician TRACK and ROPE hit size, clipping and object overlap (scripts/opera_world_hotspot_2d.gd:12-14, 43-47; scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:738-743). The TRACK surface draws three 54-pixel-radius choice circles (108-pixel diameter) while input maps x-position into one of three lanes (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1405-1411, 2849-2855). Neither actual screen scale nor hand/thumb target alignment was rendered or touched in this run.
tactile.press_response: A correct lane press emits a choice gesture; the world advances the target, calls start_shuffle, and redraws. The test log confirms the resulting state and fresh shuffle after accepted hats (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1249-1260, 2849-2855; scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3536-3548; probe log lines 717-720). The probe did not verify visible response within two rendered frames or actual contact/sound.
tactile.drag_hold_release: TRACK is a one-finger tap into one of three lanes. ROPE is a held one-finger drag along the authored arch from x=16% to x=84% of its surface; trace points outside its corridor, reverse movement, or a progress jump over 18% trigger a 0.24-second rehint and zero progress for that segment (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1676-1687, 1728-1777). Lifting ends the trace; incomplete progress returns to its demonstration state (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1234-1247). These thresholds come from code, not observed child input.
tactile.ownership: The shared gesture surface records one active touch index, ignores another press while held, routes drag only from the active index, and releases that owner's touch (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1249-1278). This source path was not exercised with physical fingers or a Magician-specific multi-touch assertion in this session.
tactile.cancellation: An incomplete ROPE lift resets its demo presentation while retaining the surface's trace progress; the tested assignment did not exercise app focus loss, pause, route cancellation, or interruption during Roshan's approach (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1234-1247; scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:1991-2028).

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: TRACK asks the child to follow a moving hat and choose a lane, then ROPE changes the verb to tracing a visible path. The two mechanics offer distinct agency, but the probe proves only state changes and not whether a child understands that the correct hat is the one to follow.
play_appeal.variety: Magician's room path includes hold, choice, trace, cabinet swipe, and circle phases (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:187-193); the assigned evidence specifically checks TRACK and ROPE. Whether these feel like satisfying different tricks rather than a series of abstract progress bars needs rendered/child observation.
play_appeal.world_response: Accepted TRACK answers move the answer cue through a visible shuffle; authored ROPE tracing moves along an arch and updates trace fill. Real hand-to-rope contact and transformation into the promised ribbon were not seen in this headless run (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5261-5284, 1676-1777; scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3518-3521).
play_appeal.replay: The phase route offers later cabinet and portal actions after rope, but the session did not reach or exit/re-enter the visible career route. A child's reason to replay TRACK/ROPE remains unknown.
play_appeal.concrete_test_or_proposal: In a short, consented Lenovo Tab M11 observation, show the ordinary Opera Hall route without coaching and note whether the child chooses the Magician portal, follows the moving TRACK hat through several shuffles, and begins ROPE from its indicated start. Test one deliberate wrong-lane tap and one coarse or reverse trace movement; record whether the current cue makes the retry obvious or the child loses the rope. Ask whether they want to repeat one trick, without suggesting the answer. If typical tracing repeatedly restarts, prototype a visibly broad corridor or forgiving resume-from-nearest-point on existing art and compare comprehension and missed-touch counts with this exact current candidate; do not alter protected voice files or treat the proposal as an accepted change.

play_sequence.input: From Opera Hall, let the child choose the painted Magician portal by touch; do not use a debug career shortcut. Continue through any earlier act beats until the TRACK phase is invited.
play_sequence.wait: Allow the portal's 0.55-second actor move and launch callback, then wait for the ordinary career object cue and Roshan's approach/opening; the 0.62-second hotspot opening is a source constant, not total travel time.
play_sequence.basis: Opera Hall connects the Magician portal button to _choose_career and launches after its actor tween (scripts/opera_house_venue_2d.gd:337-352, 405-423). Live ACTS includes the Magician career (scripts/opera_house.gd:83-88). Probe uses direct internal setup instead (scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:620-644).

play_sequence.input: When TRACK is the active invitation, tap the visible pearl_tide_pool object once.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for Roshan to reach the object and the hotspot opening to finish before touching the activity; no observed travel duration is available.
play_sequence.basis: Magician TRACK is bound to pearl_tide_pool, and the active phase arms exactly its themed object (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:417; scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:1991-2028; probe log lines 738-740).

play_sequence.input: Tap the lane showing the glowing hat, one tap per shuffle. Let the child choose the moment of each next tap.
play_sequence.wait: Pause through each 1.5-second source shuffle before offering another touch; continue until the phase completes. This is a code timer and the ordinary phase goal is six progress units, not six seconds.
play_sequence.basis: TRACK maps a press to a lane and emits only for the target; correct choices advance target and start a new shuffle (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1249-1260, 2849-2855; scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3536-3548; phase goal scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:190).

play_sequence.input: For one retry observation, tap a different lane once; then let the child tap the glowing lane when ready.
play_sequence.wait: Wait for the cue to settle before the second tap; record whether the wrong lane is visibly rejected and the correct lane is still findable. Do not claim a particular rendered response from this probe.
play_sequence.basis: Only the selected lane emits a choice event; the source keeps target selection lane-based and wrong presses do not advance the world (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1249-1260, 2849-2855).

play_sequence.input: After TRACK's completion picture, tap the newly armed teal_shell_stage invitation to reach ROPE.
play_sequence.wait: Let the 2.2-second completion picture and next invitation appear; then allow approach and the room-object opening to finish.
play_sequence.basis: ROPE maps to teal_shell_stage (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:417); shared completion holds 2.2 seconds before the next phase is armed (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3560-3598).

play_sequence.input: Press at the rope trace's current start cue, keep one finger down, and follow the arch in short forward strokes toward its end; lift only when the child pauses or the trace finishes.
play_sequence.wait: After each short stroke, wait for the fill/demo response before continuing. If the path re-prompts, let the child try again from the indicated start rather than forcing a fixed duration.
play_sequence.basis: Magician trace is an arch with 16%-84% horizontal travel; trace starts within a bounded hit rectangle and re-prompts for off-corridor, reverse, or >18% segment jumps (scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1676-1687, 1728-1777).

play_sequence.input: At the finish, stop touching and let the child view the completed rope picture; then ask whether they want another trick or to leave.
play_sequence.wait: Keep the completion image visible for its 2.2-second code hold, then observe the child's own choice without counting runner time as session length.
play_sequence.basis: Shared success accepts the picture and holds it before advancing (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3560-3574); source also defines later Magician CABINET and PORTAL phases (scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:193).

observations.title: Correct TRACK choices visibly move the answer cue into a fresh shuffle
evidence: scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3536-3548 advances the Magician choice target after a correct gesture and starts the shuffle from the previous lane.
scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:5261-5284 sets a 1.5-second shuffle and draws the answer glide/decoy arc.
scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:620-644 directly injects a correct choice and asserts the next cue and fresh shuffle state.
audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L20/attempt_1/probe.log:717-720 reports both TRACK cue and fresh-shuffle assertions OK; terminal line reports OPERA2D|result: ALL OK.
audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L20/attempt_1/receipt.json records exact engine 4.7.2-stable, isolated profile, status PASS, headless=true, and rendered_mobile_acceptance=false.
observations.reproduction: In the assigned probe, TRACK is placed in task_open state, then world._on_gesture("choice", 1.0, 1.0) is called and the target change, choice flash, shuffle timer and previous lane are asserted. This establishes internal state behavior, not visible-route child performance.
observations.child_impact: A correct choice gets an immediate next moving cue in code, which could make the follow action legible and lively. Whether the child can keep track of the correct hat during motion is unobserved.
observations.proposed_repair: No runtime repair is indicated by the assertion. Validate whether the glow remains findable through each shuffle at actual phone scale and whether an incorrect lane tap preserves a clear retry cue.
observations.acceptance_test: On the matching rendered build, follow a visible hat through a shuffle and tap its lane; verify the next correct lane cues a fresh glide, a wrong lane neither advances progress nor hides the answer, and a child can recover without reading or coaching.

observations.title: ROPE is an ordered trace with a bounded start area and a strict per-event jump cap
evidence: scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1676-1687 defines the Magician arch path and start hit rectangle (at least 38 px or 16% of the smaller surface dimension).
scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1728-1777 rejects reverse movement, points outside the trace corridor, and progress jumps greater than 0.18; accepted travel updates fill and emits swipe progress.
scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:1234-1247 ends the trace on release and reactivates its demo while incomplete.
scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:3518-3521 completes authored swipe contexts only when trace_journey reaches 1.0.
observations.reproduction: A code-grounded manual check can start at the current trace cue, move backward or jump farther than 18% of its normalized journey in one drag event, and inspect the branch that triggers _trace_rehint with no earned progress. This session did not send those actual touch events.
observations.child_impact: A child who uses one long coarse swipe or reverses direction may see the demonstration restart; this might teach the route or feel like lost work. Actual occurrence and child response require device observation.
observations.proposed_repair: Keep the ordered trace semantics, but test whether a broad visible corridor and resume-from-current-progress after release better support imperfect one-finger tracing; change only after a repeatable child/device failure is observed.
observations.acceptance_test: On a target tablet, have a child trace with natural short strokes and release/restart once. Record earned progress, restart frequency, whether the start marker is rediscovered, and whether the rope becomes one continuous ribbon; verify no passive or off-target input can finish it.

observations.child_impact: The room invitations are authored to exceed the project minimum, but a visually smaller prop or the 108-pixel choice circle could still feel difficult if rendered scale or a hand obscures its cue. No observed miss is claimed.
observations.proposed_repair: No size change is justified from this headless evidence. Capture the ordinary route at the approved aspect and inspect visible bounds and lane hit area before considering a larger affordance.
observations.acceptance_test: At native Mobile layout and on Lenovo Tab M11, confirm the TRACK and ROPE picture centers align to their touch hit regions and a child can activate each invitation/lane with one finger without thumb occlusion; retain exact screenshots and device results.
